text:
I sever my ties with the sea
+when the waters come to me.
+
+Let us always go out. Let us savor
+the stupendous song, the song uttered
+by desire’s lower lips.
+O prodigious maidenhood.
+The saltless breeze passes.
+
+Far off I scent the marrow
+hearing the deep groping, hunting
+for undertow keys.
+
+And if in this way we came nose-first
+against the absurd,
+we would cover ourselves with the gold of having nothing,
+and brood the still-unborn wing
+of night, sister
+to this orphaned wing of day,
+which by dint of being one is wing no longer.

translation.title: Trilce: Poem XLV — I Sever My Ties with the Sea
translation.editorial_note: Lower lips retain the erotic anatomy behind the song, while teclas keeps the poem’s submerged keyboard; the final single wing loses winghood through its very singularity.
